s1.syndrome_frame: subacute onset of tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core in a patient with immunocompromised state
salient_findings: tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions
sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells
key_facts: 74-year-old woman with chronic lymphocytic leukemia
complex karyotype with TP53 mutation and trisomy 12
receiving zanubrutinib and subcutaneous immunoglobulin replacement
hospitalized for pulmonary sepsis in May 2022
developed grade 4 neutropenia for over 15 days
febrile peak
skin lesions appeared on lower limbs and then upper limbs
zanubrutinib was discontinued
oral itraconazole was begun
histopathological examination showed severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation
angioinvasive microbial structures were seen
sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells were seen

shortlist.label: Mucormycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of angioinvasive microbial structures and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells in histopathological examination

shortlist.label: Entomophthoramosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of thick-walled ovoid sporangia and pauciseptate hyphae in histopathological examination, consistent with entomophthoromycosis

shortlist.label: Basidiobolomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of subacute onset of tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core, consistent with basidiobolomycosis

shortlist.label: Conidiobolomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of sparse hyphal mats and sporangial-type cells in histopathological examination, consistent with conidiobolomycosis

shortlist.label: Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised state and presence of febrile peak, although histopathological findings are not typical for aspergillosis

raw.rationale: The presence of sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells, thin-walled pauciseptate hyphae, and thick-walled ovoid sporangia in the histopathological examination are characteristic of Conidiobolomycosis, which is a rare fungal infection that can cause subcutaneous zygomycosis.

rejected.label: Mucormycosis
rejected.why: Mucormycosis typically shows wide, ribbon-like, non-septate or pauciseptate hyphae, which is not consistent with the histopathological findings in this case.

rejected.label: Entomophthoramosis
rejected.why: Entomophthoramosis is a rare fungal infection that typically affects insects, and the histopathological findings in this case do not match the typical characteristics of Entomophthoramosis.

rejected.label: Basidiobolomycosis
rejected.why: Basidiobolomycosis typically shows thick-walled, septate hyphae with a distinctive 'buddy-budding' pattern, which is not consistent with the histopathological findings in this case.

rejected.label: Aspergillosis
rejected.why: Aspergillosis typically shows septate, branching hyphae with a characteristic 'V' or 'Y' shape, which is not consistent with the histopathological findings in this case.
